minutes.headline: Task force drafted its Town Meeting pitch for a stormwater utility fee, floating figures under $100/year but not committing.
minutes.summary: The Stormwater Task Force spent most of the meeting editing its slide deck for the upcoming Annual Town Meeting presentation, researching MS4 non-compliance fine ranges and debating how to describe a proposed tiered stormwater utility fee for homeowners and businesses without committing to specific dollar figures. It approved the prior meeting's minutes, got an update that soil conditions may force a redesign of the library stormwater BMP project, and voted to adjourn.

what_happened.line: The task force decided against naming a specific dollar figure for a proposed homeowner stormwater utility fee, opting for a "less than" framing instead.
It also chose to present that fee as a projected quarterly amount rather than an annual one, judging it more palatable to residents.
Members want the fee billed through the existing property tax bill rather than a separate mailing, pending confirmation with the town treasurer.
Soil test pits may force a redesign of the library stormwater project, the group was told.
The group approved its prior meeting's minutes and voted to adjourn.

why_it_matters: If adopted, a stormwater utility fee would be a new charge added to residents' and businesses' property tax bills, tiered by lot or impervious surface area.
This fee has not been set or voted on; it is being shaped for a warrant article at the upcoming Annual Town Meeting, where residents will get a vote.
How the fee is billed and administered still depends on confirmation from the town treasurer, so the mechanics remain unsettled.
